Estimate Optimal SLURM Array Resources from a Micro-Pilot

Source: R/resources.R
estimate_resources.Rd

Fits an empirical runtime and memory scaling model from a pilot_run() result and computes optimal SLURM array chunking (--array), memory ceiling (--mem), walltime limit (--time), and CPU allocation (--cpus-per-task) with configurable safety margins and queue-friendly rounding.

Usage

estimate_resources(
  pilot,
  n_tasks = pilot$meta$n_total_hint,
  target_chunk_minutes = 15,
  max_array_size = 1000L,
  min_chunk_size = 1L,
  max_chunk_size = NULL,
  mem_safety = 1.35,
  time_safety = 1.5,
  mem_min_mb = 512L,
  mem_round_mb = 256L,
  time_min_minutes = 5,
  time_round_minutes = 5,
  cpus_per_task = NULL,
  parallel_efficiency = 0.85,
  partition = NULL,
  account = NULL,
  qos = NULL,
  max_concurrent = NULL,
  strategy = c("contiguous", "round_robin", "lpt"),
  task_weights = NULL
)

Arguments

pilot

A slurmpilot_pilot object returned by pilot_run().

n_tasks

Positive integer total number of tasks in the full workload. Defaults to pilot$meta$n_total_hint.

target_chunk_minutes

Target walltime in minutes per SLURM array task. Default 15.

max_array_size

Maximum number of SLURM array indices allowed by the cluster (MaxArraySize). Default 1000L.

min_chunk_size

Minimum tasks per SLURM array chunk. Default 1L.

max_chunk_size

Optional maximum tasks per SLURM array chunk.

mem_safety

Multiplicative safety factor applied to predicted peak RSS. Default 1.35.

time_safety

Multiplicative safety factor applied to predicted upper walltime. Default 1.50.

mem_min_mb

Minimum requested memory in MB. Default 512L.

mem_round_mb

Granularity in MB to round requested memory up to. Default 256L.

time_min_minutes

Minimum requested walltime in minutes. Default 5.

time_round_minutes

Granularity in minutes to round requested walltime up to. Default 5.

cpus_per_task

Optional integer CPU count per SLURM array task. Defaults to pilot$meta$cpus_per_task.

parallel_efficiency

Numeric in (0, 1] specifying Amdahl parallel efficiency when scaling cpus_per_task beyond the pilot CPU count. Default 0.85.

partition

Optional SLURM --partition name.

account

Optional SLURM --account name.

qos

Optional SLURM --qos name.

max_concurrent

Optional positive integer array concurrency cap (--array=1-M%max_concurrent).

strategy

Chunk assignment strategy: "contiguous" (default), "round_robin", or "lpt" (Longest Processing Time first load balancing for heterogeneous task workloads).

task_weights

Optional positive numeric vector of length n_tasks providing relative per-task runtime/cost weights for "lpt" load balancing. When strategy = "lpt" and task_weights = NULL, weights are interpolated linearly from the pilot trials across 1:n_tasks (or fall back to uniform weights if fewer than 2 distinct pilot indices exist).

Value

An S3 object of class "slurmpilot_resources" containing computed chunking, SLURM resource values, formatted flags (slurm_flags), partition table (chunks), and diagnostic scaling estimates (estimates).

Details

For a chunk of \(k\) sequential tasks on \(c\) CPUs (relative to pilot CPU count \(c_0\) with Amdahl parallel efficiency \(\eta\)):

  • Relative speedup is \(S = ((1 - \eta) + \eta / c_0) / ((1 - \eta) + \eta / c)\).

  • Optimal chunk size \(k^*\) balances target chunk duration (target_chunk_minutes) against startup overhead amortization and max_array_size.

  • Chunk walltime upper bound combines CLT standard-deviation scaling (\(\sqrt{k^*}\sigma_t\)) with Fenton-Wilkinson log-normal and nonparametric upper-quantile protection plus time_safety.

  • Chunk memory accounts for baseline RSS, peak net working set, modest logarithmic heap fragmentation across sequential replications (\(1 + 0.05 \log_2(k^*)\)), and mem_safety.

See also

pilot_run(), resource_spec(), plan_chunks(), as_slurm_flags()

Examples

args <- lapply(1:10, function(i) list(n = 200, seed = i))
pilot <- pilot_run(
  fun = function(x) {
    set.seed(x$seed)
    mean(rnorm(x$n))
  },
  args_list = args,
  n_pilot = 2L
)
res <- estimate_resources(pilot, n_tasks = 500L, target_chunk_minutes = 5)
print(res)
#> 
#> ── slurmpilot SLURM Resource Plan 
#> • Workload: 500 tasks -> 1 array chunks (500 tasks/chunk)
#> • SLURM flags: --array=1 --cpus-per-task=1 --mem=512M --time=00:05:00
#> ℹ Predicted chunk walltime: 1.3s (expected 1.2s, startup overhead 59.3%)
#> ℹ Predicted peak RSS: 130.8 MB -> requested 512M
#> ℹ Estimated total compute: 0.00 CPU-hours
